dialog.body: Zoning and Inspections, this is Anita. How can I help you?
Hi, yes. Good morning. [pause] I'm, um, I'm trying to buy a shed. One of those prefab ones, it comes already built, they drop it off. And I don't know what I need from you first.
Okay, sure. So a prefab shed, delivered whole. Do you know roughly how big it is? Length and width, and whether it sits on a foundation or just on blocks or gravel?

Um, hang on. I have the paper here somewhere. [pause] Ten by twelve, I think. Or twelve by ten, same thing, I guess. And I don't know about the foundation. I think it just sits on the ground. They said something about a gravel pad.
Okay, ten by twelve is a hundred and twenty square feet. That size is where a lot of towns start asking for a permit, so it's worth doing this properly. Is this at a home or at a business?
It's, uh, a business. Well, it's behind the shop. I own a small shop. [sigh] The lot has a little yard in back, and the shed would go along the side, kind of near the line with the neighbor.
Okay. That's really the main question then, how close to the property line. Is that what you wanted to ask about, the setbacks?
Yes, the setbacks. How far from the lot line does it have to be? I measured about three feet from the fence, but I don't know if the fence is on the line or not.

Right, and that's a common problem. A fence isn't always sitting on the actual boundary. The setback depends on the zoning district your property is in, and commercial and residential districts are different. I can't give you a number until I know which district you're in. Do you have the street address handy?

I do, but, um, I'd rather not say it right now, I'm in the car and, ah, the app just froze. I was looking at the shed company's app, with the order. Hold on. [pause] It's stuck on a white screen. I have to restart it.
No problem, take your time. Are you driving? I don't want you fiddling with it on the road.
No, no, I'm parked. Outside the shop. [sigh] Okay, it's coming back. It's loading. Sorry.

That's fine. While that loads, here's the general picture. Usually the setback for a small accessory building like a shed is smaller than for the main building, but it's not zero, and it's measured from the actual lot line, not the fence. So if you're not sure where the line is, you may need your survey or plot plan.
A survey. I think I have one from when I bought the place. Is that the, the map with the little numbers on the edges?

Yes, that's probably it. It shows the boundary lengths and where the building sits. If you've got that, bring a copy, or a photo of it, and mark where the shed would go and how far it is from each line.
Okay. And so I need a shed permit? That's the type? I wasn't sure if it was a building permit or a zoning permit or, I don't know, two different things.

Good question. For your purposes you're applying for a shed permit. Zoning looks at the placement, the setbacks, and the building side looks at how it's put together. You don't need to file two separate things, it goes through together in one application.
Oh. So one application. I thought I had to go to one office, then the other office. [sigh] That's better.
Just the one. Now, you said it's delivered built. Does the company give you a spec sheet or drawing of the shed? That usually gets attached.
The app has something. A PDF, I think. It says, um, dimensions and the height. Do I print it?
You can print it, or upload it if you apply online. Either way works. Include the height and the dimensions, and a simple sketch of the lot with the shed marked on it.
Okay. And how long does it take? For them to say yes? Because the company wants to deliver in, I think, three weeks. Or four. I'd have to look again.

For a simple shed it's usually not a long wait, but it depends how busy we are and whether the application is complete. If something's missing, the clock basically stops until we get it. I'd say don't lock in the delivery date until you've got approval in hand.
So don't schedule it yet. Okay. They did want a deposit, though. [sigh] Is that a problem?

That's between you and the company, but I'd ask them if the deposit is refundable or if the date can move, in case the permit takes longer than planned. Or in case the setback means the shed has to sit somewhere else on the lot.
Somewhere else. Right. I didn't think about that. So three feet might not be enough.

It might be, it might not. That's why I'd like to look up your district. When you're ready with the address, call back or come by the office and we'll pull it up on the map. Or if you give it to me now, I can check while you're on the line.
Um, I think I'll come by. I'd rather have the survey with me. Is it, ah, open all day?
We're here weekdays during regular City Hall hours, and the counter is open this morning and this afternoon. Ask for zoning at the desk and they'll send you my way.
Okay. So, to say it back. Ten by twelve, bring the survey, the paper from the shed company, a sketch. One shed permit. And don't pick the delivery date yet.
That's it exactly. And it helps if you can tell me where the shed's door faces and what it's made of, wood or metal or resin.
Wood, I think. The app says wood. Let me check. [pause] Yes, wood. Door on the short side.
Perfect, write that on your sketch. Anything else I can answer?
No, I think that's all. I was lost before I called. Still a little, but less. Thank you.
You're welcome. Come on in with your paperwork and we'll sort out the rest. Have a good day.
You too. Thanks.
